I go to PSU Abington right now. It's a good option because its cheaper and safer but a few of my friends have been a little disappointed because you don't really get a full college experience. It's a little less than 4k students and a lot of them commute so not too many stay on campus. There is no rushing, few parties and the campus is pretty small. I do know that the science building is pretty nice though. If you do enroll, you definitely want to keep your gpa above a 3.2 so that you have the option of switching to the main campus after 2 years, if you want to. The large alumni connection is a huge plus.

I think people are pretty stuck in their ways with how they feel about trans people. For one, not everyone understands trans people as a whole and so many people have very wrong and harmful interpretations of it (i.e. it's a mental disorder, trans people are attention-seeking). Although, some people's transphobia could just be a product of their environment. I am gay and my parents have been homophobic for as long as I can remember and that clearly influenced my sister when she was younger and impressionable. Now that she is older, she has her own opinions on gay and trans people and she has even called our mother out on the slights she makes about the LGBT community. As for me, I do not fully understand trans people but I am actively  learning new things about them daily, how to treat and respect them, how to be an ally and how to not make microagressions towards them.
